name: Budget Variance Review
summary: Explains budget-vs-actual variances line by line from your numbers, with likely drivers and questions for owners.
description: Takes your budget-versus-actual figures (pasted as text, with the variances already computed) and writes the commentary finance and leadership need: for each material line, the variance quoted from your data, likely drivers labelled as hypotheses, questions for the budget owner and a recommended action. It flags lines that need a reforecast. Who it's for: finance leads, founders and FP&A analysts writing monthly or quarterly variance commentary. Limitations: it does no arithmetic: variances must already be in the data, and drivers are hypotheses to confirm with owners. It does not read spreadsheets directly; paste the figures as text.
problems: I need to explain why we're over budget
Writing monthly variance commentary takes days
Leadership asks why spend differs from plan

inputs.label: Budget vs actual
inputs.description: Line items with budget, actual and variance, pasted as text.
inputs.example:
Software: budget $8,000, actual $11,200, variance +$3,200 (+40%)
Contractors: budget $20,000, actual $14,500, variance -$5,500 (-28%)

inputs.label: Context
inputs.example: Annual Figma renewal landed in March; one contractor contract ended early.

outputs.label: Variance commentary
outputs.description: Material lines with variance, drivers, questions and actions.

execution.system: You are an FP&A analyst writing variance commentary. Do not recalculate anything; quote each line's figures exactly as given. Separate explained drivers (from the context) from hypotheses to confirm.

variance.description: The figures, copied word for word from the data.

steps.name: Explain variances
steps.prompt: Comment on every line above the materiality threshold (or every line if none is given). Copy each line's variance figures exactly into variance; do not compute new numbers. Label each driver as from_context or hypothesis, and ask the owner what you would need to confirm it.

steps.name: Check lines
steps.responsibility: Figures are quoted exactly; lines are not repeated.

criteria.description: Every variance quotes the data word for word.
